headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors when Kotaemon ingests Argo Workflows outputs into a shared file-backed RAG workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can emit workflow artifacts over REST/gRPC and B ingests documents, PDFs, HTML, and chat transcripts via a web UI and local app data. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if A’s outputs are fed into B’s corpus or copied into its workspace. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty is not enough to lower severity.
conditions: IF A-generated artifacts are imported into B's indexed documents or chat corpus
IF B treats file contents as trusted instructions during retrieval or summarization
mitigations: Separate A output folders from B ingestion paths
Disable automatic indexing of A-produced artifacts
Add a manual review step before B ingests workflow outputs
Tag A outputs as untrusted in the RAG pipeline
requires-engineering: enforce provenance filtering in B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted egress; B handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and writes to ./ktem_app_data while calling third-party LLM APIs. If they share a workspace or if A’s artifacts contain sensitive parameters, B can leak them through uploads or retrieval prompts. The shared-pathway is plausible from profiles alone, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF A artifacts or parameters are placed in B's indexed workspace
IF B sends retrieved context to OpenAI, AzureOpenAI, Cohere, Groq, or similar APIs
mitigations: Keep A artifacts out of B's ./ktem_app_data directory
Redact parameters before indexing
Restrict B to local-only models for sensitive corpora
Rotate any API keys exposed in B's corpus
requires-engineering: add DLP filters before outbound prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes API-based workflow execution and allowlisted egress, while B supports multiple instances and writes to a local app-data directory. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, git state, or shared OAuth scopes, so direct conflict is not established. Any conflict would require an unusual shared deployment setup.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or database
IF an orchestrator launches multiple B instances against shared mutable state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Avoid shared databases or git repos
Check for lock files before concurrent runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces workflow artifacts that B can ingest, summarize, and cite. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative without verification, errors in A can cascade into B’s answers or downstream actions. B’s RAG-style document handling makes this plausible by default, though the profiles do not prove a fully automated action chain.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated artifacts as retrieved evidence without verification
IF B forwards summaries or citations from A into user-facing answers
mitigations: Require source verification before B cites A outputs
Mark A outputs as untrusted evidence
Add a human review gate for high-impact responses
Compare A outputs against original upstream data
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware retrieval

E_compliance.rationale: A is docs-only open-source workflow software with artifacts/parameters, while B handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and can send content to third-party LLM APIs. If regulated or sensitive data from A enters B’s corpus, B’s outbound API calls can create retention and residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR boundaries, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data from A is indexed or queried in B
IF B routes that data to external model APIs with different retention terms
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B ingestion
Use a local model backend for sensitive queries
Document retention settings for B's API providers
Purge B app data after each review cycle
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
